status: launch path length effect reproduced; source attribution pending normalized launch comparison
observations: R111 uses 4.324% fewer user instructions than its R110-A control at low connections and 4.296% fewer at 64 connections in the first ablation series.
However R110-A itself shifted from about 8914.63 to 9435.16 user instructions/send at low connections between the two series, with identical ELF/helper hashes. R109 remained about 8645.64.

R110-A launched from a 50-byte path in the original series and a 41-byte path in the ablation series. main retains argv Strings for the daemon lifetime. Startup allocation state is a hypothesis, not an established cause.
Do not use the observed 4.3% as an isolated lookup effect until all subjects have the same launch-name length and path sensitivity has been calibrated.
runtime: Accepted R109 unchanged; experimental R111 worktree preserved, no further runtime variant now.
path_calibration: Four same-ELF pairs reproduced lower counts for 50-byte than 41-byte launch paths: median -5.517% user instructions; typical counts 8914.62 vs 9435.17. One long-path sample was 9018.66, also retained. This isolates a launch-path dependence, not its allocator mechanism.
